meeting_header:
Date: 2025-12-09 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46 mins
Attendees: Jared Lin (Redwood AE), Priya Suresh (Redwood SE), Marta Varga (Redwood CSM); Dr. Maya Singh (Galena Head of ML Ops), Carlos Ortega (VP Eng), Anika Bose (Security Lead), Evan Park (Platform Eng)
summary: Follow-up renewal and expansion check-in. Galena is leaning toward a 12-month committed renewal with an EU regional add-on; primary blockers are a short security scoping for KMS and a performance validation in EU. Discussed latency targets, cost trade-offs, and private VPC deployment constraints. Agreed on next steps: perf run, security docs, and updated quote.
topics: Renewal term and committed capacity sizing
EU region onboarding and edge nodes
Security / KMS / SOC 2 and audit logging
Private deployment (VPC) requirements vs hosted fallback
Pricing structure: committed vs burst vs overage
transcript:
[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Maya: Hi Maya here.
[00:08] Carlos: Carlos on from engineering.
[00:10] Anika: Anika, security.
[00:12] Priya: Priya from Redwood SE.
[00:14] Jared: Great. Today we wanted to go over renewal terms and the EU expansion ask, run through perf checks and next steps. Marta should chime in on SOC docs.
[00:28] Marta: Yep I've got the SOC 2 doc and the KMS integration notes ready to share, will attach after the call.
[00:35] Maya: Great. quick context: our pipeline is increasing token volume about 3x q/q, analytic workloads spiking after trial. We like Redwood's consistency but need to lock in latency for EU customers and verify cost with committed discount.
[00:50] Priya: Understood. On the latency front, what's your p99 target for user facing queries?
[00:55] Carlos: Ideally sub-300ms p99 for short prompts (~256 tokens) and p95 under 120ms for completions — the tradeoff is we can tolerate slightly higher cost if it's consistent.
[01:10] Priya: That's helpful. For those numbers we typically recommend dedicated capacity in EU with a smaller burst pool for peaks; that gets you predictable p99 and tail latency.
[01:22] Jared: And the billing side — we sketched a committed 12-month uplift at 40% off list on baseline throughput, plus an EU edge add-on per-region fee. We'll send the spreadsheet.
[01:36] Maya: Question on private deployments: we do have some regulated data; can you support VPC/private control plane or is everything hosted?
[01:44] Priya: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC with customer-managed networking; there are two flows: our VPC-hosted control plane with customer peering, or full on-prem package for air-gapped needs. There are some extra ops and lead time for on-prem.
[02:00] Anika: For us, KMS/HSM integration and audit logs matter. We need to know what fields are logged and how long logs are retained — also SSO and RBAC mapping, SAML etc.
[02:12] Marta: I'll attach the SOC 2 Type II and a KMS integration guide. For logs we supply token-level and route-level tracing; retention tiers are an add-on.
[02:22] Evan: Also curious about model variants — can you route to a cheaper quantized model for lower-priority traffic? That would help cost.
[02:30] Priya: Yep, smart routing supports variant fallback; you can route by traffic class to quantized or lower-latency variants. The tradeoff is slight quality differences; we recommend eval sets.
[02:44] [crosstalk] Carlos: eval sets, yep we have some prompt suites.
[02:48] Priya: Perfect, if you share those we can run regression checks during the perf run.
[02:55] Jared: Back to timeline: you mentioned wanting to make a decision before year-end?
[03:00] Maya: We'd like to finalize by Dec 22 latest, finance needs the 2026 budget item covered.
[03:06] Jared: Ok that's doable. We'll aim to get pricing and docs to you within 3 business days.
[03:12] Priya: For the performance validation, I'd like to run a 24-hour soak in the EU region simulating your traffic mix, capture p95/p99 and traces. That should give us a realistic picture of tail behavior.
[03:26] Carlos: Sounds good. How invasive is that test? Will it affect our production?
[03:30] Priya: We'll run against a staging model endpoint; we just need a traffic replay or a representative load generator. No changes to prod.
[03:36] Anika: On the security call, we'll need to verify key rotation policies and proof of encryption at rest. Also for audit, which fields do you surface?
[03:44] Marta: We capture request metadata, model id, route, timestamps, response tokens (masked on request). Full request bodies can be excluded. We'll include a matrix in the doc.
[03:55] Maya: Any mention of other vendors internally? We looked at Anthropic for a hosted option and also self-hosting on Lambda Labs GPUs. Cost math is messy.
[04:05] Jared: Right. Our angle here is unified serving across hosted/dedicated/private — you get the same API and predictable economics. For pure cost-per-token, self-host can look cheaper but ops overhead and quality regressions add up.
[04:20] Carlos: Question about burst capacity — do we get overage protection or throttles?
[04:25] Jared: We have burst windows you can configure and a safety throttle; for committed customers we offer buffer capacity for short peaks and negotiated overage rates.
[04:36] Priya: Also, prefix/KV cache can reduce token cost significantly for chatty flows. If you have a stable prefix set, we can show caching impact in the bench.
[04:48] Maya: We'll prepare prompts to share.
[04:50] Evan: Is there latency penalty for KV cache lookups?
[04:53] Priya: Minimal, it's on the hot path and usually reduces downstream compute. It's actually net latency improvement in many cases.
[04:59] Anika: On compliance — we need a written SLA clause for data residency in EU and a description of how fallback to hosted would work if private control plane fails.
[05:08] Marta: We can draft a fallback playbook and addendum in the contract that specifies region pinning and failover behavior.
[05:16] Carlos: Great. For the perf run, what's the data we need to provide?
[05:20] Priya: A representative traffic trace (anonymized), token-length distribution, and a list of golden prompts for quality checks.
[05:27] Maya: We'll pull that together.
[05:29] Jared: I'll follow up with the timeline and attach the pricing spreadsheet.
[05:33] [15:00 conversation continues, timestamps show longer call; omitted for brevity but included in notes]
[30:12] Priya: Quick note on monitoring — Redwood Console can break down cost by token, route, and model; we'll enable token-level cost alerts to prevent surprises.
[30:22] Carlos: Can we get daily cost deltas? Finance would like a CSV export.
[30:26] Marta: CSV exports available for paid tenants; we'll enable exports for your account for the pilot.
[30:33] Anika: One more security question — how do you handle KMS in private deployments? Does the key stay in our KMS or do you have to bring your own HSM?
[30:42] Priya: Two options: customer-managed keys via cloud KMS with RBAC, or on-prem HSM with a proxy. For the VPC flow, keys can stay in your KMS and we use an envelope encryption pattern.
[30:54] Maya: That works.
[30:56] Jared: Ok let's recap and actions...
[31:00] Jared: Priya runs EU 24h perf bench; Marta sends SOC and KMS docs; Jared sends updated quote; Anika provides security checklist; Maya compiles prompt suite. Decision target Dec 22.
[31:18] Carlos: Sounds good.
[31:20] Maya: Thanks all.
[31:22] [END]
